newsitem.title: USA: Ferber case warning to muni industry - SEC official.
newsitem.headline: Ferber case warning to muni industry - SEC official.

text.p: Juan Marcelino, head of the Securities and Exchange Commission's Boston district office, called Thursday's settlement agreement with municipal banker Mark Ferber another warning shot to the municipal bond industry.
"This matter demonstrates the Commission's concern regarding abusive practices in the municipal industry," Marcelino said in a telephone interview with Reuters.

As part of his agreement with the SEC, Ferber will pay $650,000 in penalties. In papers filed at the U.S. District Court in Boston, Ferber also accepted an order that permanently bars him from the municipal bond industry. The settlement does not constitute an admission or denial of wrongdoing.
Marcelino said that the SEC "will continue to move aggressively against shady practices in this industry in order to uphold the integrity of the municipal market."

The SEC said Ferber should have disclosed to his former employer Lazard Freres' advisory clients that the firm had a lucrative $5.8 million "fee-splitting" contract with Merrill Lynch & Co that resulted "in a substantial financial benefit to Ferber."
Also on Thursday, a federal judge in Boston sentenced Ferber to 33 months in prison and two years' probation and fined him $1 million in connection with the fee-splitting matter.
"We've brought cases regarding all types of issues whether it's pay-to-play or straightforward disclosure issues," Marcelino said."

"This particular action emphasizes that material financial arrangements among parties involved in issuance of municipal securities could be critical to the evaluation of an offering and, consequently, must be disclosed," Marcelino said.
Pay-to-play refers to giving of political contributions to state and local government officials in return for bond business.
Asked whether SEC will bring action against others connected to Ferber, Marcelino said, "This action today concludes the Commission's investigation of this matter."
